_note: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for slop markers. Pointed two directions: (1) DETECTION — read by the ai-slop skill at evaluate time (Decompose); (2) PREVENTION — the `ban` + `instead` fields become the intent-prep negative-constraint list at generate time. Never fork this file. Sources: claude-default (ai-tells catalog), cartoon-slop (ai-tells 'NOT from me', but PRIMARY slop for this corpus), corpus (Eman's verbatim exemplar captions). A single marker is NEVER a flag — the Judge flags only on CONVERGENCE (multiple co-occurring).
convergence_rule: Report every marker found as an observation. Slop becomes a Judge flag only when >=3 markers co-occur OR >=2 high-weight markers co-occur. State which markers drove it so a human can sanity-check. Minimalism/restraint with ONE marker is not slop.

markers.label: Gradient fill on text
visual_cues: headline or label letters filled with a color gradient
markers.instead: Solid ink color; create emphasis with weight, size, or a single accent color.

markers.label: Gradient-filled buttons / CTAs
visual_cues: primary buttons with a two-color gradient fill
markers.instead: Solid fill in one brand/accent color; differentiate primary vs secondary by fill vs outline, not by gradient.

markers.label: Purple/blue (or hot-pink) gradient background
visual_cues: large purple→blue or pink gradient wash, often behind a dark hero
markers.instead: A considered palette tied to the brand; flat surfaces or a subtle single-hue treatment with real intent.

markers.label: Default dark mode with light/glow effect
visual_cues: dark background with a soft glow/light bloom behind the hero — 'AI forward'
markers.instead: Choose light or dark for a reason; if dark, carry structure with surfaces/typography, not a glow.

markers.label: Poorly-executed glass / frosted panels
visual_cues: semi-transparent frosted panels that feel shabby / borders that don't match the theme
markers.ban: No glassmorphism unless it is executed with real craft and matches the theme.
markers.instead: Solid surfaces with deliberate elevation (shadow or border) consistent with the rest of the UI.

markers.label: AI-generated imagery that looks AI-made
visual_cues: images too perfect / uncanny, no human touch, generic stock-AI look
markers.ban: No imagery that reads as generic AI output.
markers.instead: Imagery with intent and human touch (texture, real photography, illustration, or AI art styled so it doesn't read as AI — e.g. anime/pixel/editorial treatment).

markers.label: Too many typefaces (>3)
visual_cues: 4+ distinct typefaces competing on one screen
markers.instead: One or two families; create variety with weight and size, not new fonts.

markers.label: Generic pill badge with leading dot
visual_cues: small rounded pill ('New'/'Beta'/'Live') with a colored dot at the top of the hero
markers.instead: If you need a label, set it typographically in the brand voice — or drop it.

markers.label: Three-equal-card feature grid
visual_cues: three identical-weight cards in a row, icon + heading + 2 lines
markers.instead: Vary card weight/size to express hierarchy, or use a layout that fits the actual content.

markers.label: Lucide icon in a tinted rounded square
visual_cues: row of small tinted squares each holding a thin line icon
markers.instead: Icons that carry brand character, or no icons; let typography and layout do the work.

markers.label: Cream bg + italic serif accent + tracked-uppercase eyebrow
visual_cues: warm off-white page, one italic serif 'feeling' word in a sans headline, tiny tracked-uppercase label above headings
markers.ban: Not the cream + italic-serif + eyebrow editorial-minimalism reflex repeated across sections.
markers.instead: Pick a distinctive type system and palette tied to the brand; one italic accent once is fine, the repeated trifecta is the tell.

markers.label: Generic / template feel — no personality
visual_cues: nothing brand-specific; could be any product; 'no character', static, un-imaginative
markers.instead: Inject brand personality — distinctive type, color, layout move, or motif that could only belong to this product.

markers.label: Inconsistent / too-many button styles
visual_cues: several different button shapes/styles on one screen
markers.instead: One primary, one secondary, one tertiary — a single consistent button system.

markers.label: Heading and CTA text the same size
visual_cues: no size contrast between the headline and the button/CTA text
markers.ban: Don't size the CTA the same as the heading.
markers.instead: Establish clear type hierarchy — headline dominant, CTA sized for action, body subordinate.

markers.label: Low-visibility / low-contrast text
visual_cues: text that's hard to read — light gray on white, text lost over an image
markers.instead: Meet WCAG AA (4.5:1 / 3:1 large); over images use an overlay/scrim so text stays legible.

markers.label: Poor / unbalanced padding
visual_cues: cramped or unbalanced padding inside cards/buttons; text touching edges
markers.instead: Consistent spacing on a clear scale; give content breathing room on all sides.

markers.label: Emoji used as UI icons
code_cues: unicode emoji characters in markup, esp. in icon slots (⛅ 📊 🔁 ✨ 🚀 ✅ etc.)
visual_cues: emoji standing in for icons in feature cards / lists / buttons
markers.ban: No emoji used as UI icons.
markers.instead: A single consistent custom or line-icon set with brand character; if you can't make icons, use none.

markers.label: Tracked-uppercase eyebrow label above headings
code_cues: text-transform:uppercase + letter-spacing on a small label directly above a heading
visual_cues: small tracked-uppercase label (often accent-colored) sitting above section headings, repeated section after section
markers.ban: No tracked-uppercase eyebrow/kicker label above every heading.
markers.instead: Let the headline carry the section; if you need a label, set it in the brand voice and use it sparingly, not as a per-section reflex.

markers.label: Em-dash used as a rhythmic copy tic
code_cues: repeated '—' (em-dash) in headline/body copy used for cadence rather than clause separation
visual_cues: multiple em-dashes across hero/section copy giving the templated AI-marketing cadence
markers.ban: No em-dashes as decorative rhythmic cadence in copy.
markers.instead: Write in plain sentences; use a period or a comma. Reserve the em-dash for genuine parenthetical breaks, not as a tic.

markers.label: Generic AI marketing copy (triplet taglines / soft over-promises)
code_cues: triplet parallel-verb taglines ('Build faster. Ship smarter. Sleep better.')
soft over-promise words: effortless, seamless, delightful, thoughtful, reimagined, crafted, calm
'The X for Y who Z' subhead formula
visual_cues: copy that could belong to any product; no specific, concrete claims
markers.ban: No generic triplet taglines or soft over-promise vocabulary.
markers.instead: Write specific, concrete copy about what this product actually does and for whom.

markers.label: Centered hero over a dark mesh / aurora background
code_cues: centered hero text-align:center over a dark bg with radial/mesh/aurora gradients or blurred blobs
absolute blur-3xl opacity- behind a centered hero
visual_cues: a centered headline+subhead+CTA pair floating over a dark mesh/aurora/blob background — the canonical AI hero
markers.ban: No centered hero floating over a dark mesh/aurora background.
markers.instead: Compose the hero deliberately (asymmetry, a real product visual, a brand motif); if dark, carry it with structure, not a mesh wash.

markers.label: Reflexive Inter + slate-900 + default-component look
code_cues: Inter (or Geist) as the only font + slate/zinc/neutral-900 text + untouched shadcn/Tailwind defaults
visual_cues: the unmistakable 'default modern SaaS template' look — nothing brand-specific, could be any Vercel starter
markers.ban: No reflexive Inter+slate-900 default-component look with zero brand customization.
markers.instead: Choose type and color that carry the brand; if using a component library, restyle it so it doesn't read as the default.
